summary:
The starting-pitcher category is the day's clearest fade signal across the board. All three ratings are cold on SP right now — R2 at 43% (n=190, -6.5pts), R1 identical at 43% (-6.5pts), and R3 at 46% (-5.4pts) — meaning any pick leaning on SP-driven confidence should be discounted regardless of which rating generated it. R2's runs category is the more alarming trend, sliding to 46% over the last 14 days (-6.0pts) and now riding a brutal 7-game losing streak, the same skid infecting R3's runs cell. Trends remains the one category holding steady everywhere — 53% across all three ratings over 14 days, right in line with its 54% season number — and it's the backbone of the best category combos: trends+runs leads the board at 54.1% (219-186, n=405), with trends+sp and trends+bullpen close behind. Lean into trends-anchored combos today and treat standalone SP or runs signals as noise.

Strong-play units confirm the pain is recent, not structural. All three ratings show negative net units over the last 30 days — R1 at -11.0u (89-101), R2 at -14.0u (85-95), R3 barely positive at +3.0u — a sharp reversal from healthy season-long profits (+15.0u, +15.0u, +22.0u respectively). R3 is the least damaged of the three lately and worth slightly more trust on strong plays today. On team trends, ride the model's favorites with disciplined sizing: TBR is elite when picked, 24-10 (71%) and an exceptional 18-5 (78%, +22.0u) on strong plays — the best combination of volume and unit profit on the board. BOS (72%, n=36) and LAD strong plays (86%, +15.0u) also stand out as green lights. Fade HOU on strong plays specifically — 3-8 (27%, -8.0u) is a glaring red flag despite a respectable overall 57% mark, suggesting the model's conviction reads are backwards on Houston lately.
